pages.lesson:
LESSON: MASS

Grade: PP2
Subject: MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.2: Mass

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Mass. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. compare heavy and light objects in the environment
2. appreciate objects of different mass in their environment 68 e) enjoy manipulating objects of different mass in daily life experiences measuring heavy and light objects

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. compare heavy and light objects in the environment
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to compare heavy and light objects in the environment. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. appreciate objects of different mass in their environment 68 e) enjoy manipulating objects of different mass in daily life experiences measuring heavy and light objects
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to appreciate objects of different mass in their environment 68 e) enjoy manipulating objects of different mass in daily life experiences measuring heavy and light objects. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market in your county, count 10 mangoes. Put them in 2 groups of 5. That is sorting and grouping.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row. Write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and your parent gives you 5 more, you have 12 shillings. That is addition.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Mass.
2. Explain Mass to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Mass.
4. Show that you can: compare heavy and light objects in the environment
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Mass. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Mass important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. compare heavy and light objects in the environment
2. appreciate objects of different mass in their environment 68 e) enjoy manipulating objects of different mass in daily life experiences measuring heavy and light objects

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Learner lesson
